condition.purpose: Establish whether the specified actual-rent evidence is documented for use of actual rents that exceed market rents, without resolving the source's stated question about which rent rule applies.

condition.purpose: Establish the applicable value basis and 65% maximum LTV / CLTV for loans on properties considered listed for sale under the stated timing rule.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal report, listing history, and loan application for the appraised value, lowest recent listing price, and Application Date.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the property was listed for sale in the last six months, measured from the last date of being listed to the Application Date.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: For a property within that listing period, verify that the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% and is based on the lesser of the appraised value or the lowest recent listing price.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the stated listing-period value basis and maximum are met.

condition.purpose: Establish whether the property type is eligible under the listed property types and, for the property types with printed limits, whether the applicable CLTV limit and stated conditions are met.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal report and loan application for property type, state, transaction purpose, CLTV, and any applicable DSCR information.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the property type is among SFR, Townhome, PUD, Warrantable Condo, Non-Warrantable Condo, Condotel / PUDtel, 2-4 Units, or Manufactured.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: For Non-Warrantable Condo, verify the printed limits of 80% Purchase, 75% Refi R/T, and 75% Refi C/O; apply -5% CLTV for Florida properties and verify Min DSCR: 1.0. For Condotel / PUDtel, verify the printed limits of 75% Purchase, 70% Refi R/T, and 65% Refi C/O; apply -5% CLTV for Florida properties and verify Min DSCR: 1.0. For 2-4 Unit, verify Max CLTV: 80%. For Manufactured Home, verify 65% Purchase, 60% Refi R/T, and 60% Refi C/O. Do not assign a purpose split to the printed 2-4 Unit limit.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the property type and any applicable printed CLTV limits and conditions are met.
checks: The property type is one of the listed eligible property types: SFR, Townhome, PUD, Warrantable Condo, Non-Warrantable Condo, Condotel / PUDtel, 2-4 Units, or Manufactured.
For a Non-Warrantable Condo, CLTV does not exceed the applicable printed limit: 80% Purchase, 75% Refi R/T, or 75% Refi C/O, reduced by -5% CLTV for Florida properties; Min DSCR: 1.0.
For a Condotel / PUDtel, CLTV does not exceed the applicable printed limit: 75% Purchase, 70% Refi R/T, or 65% Refi C/O, reduced by -5% CLTV for Florida properties; Min DSCR: 1.0.
For a 2-4 Unit property, CLTV does not exceed Max CLTV: 80%.
For a Manufactured Home, CLTV does not exceed the applicable printed limit: 65% Purchase, 60% Refi R/T, or 60% Refi C/O.

outcomes.criterion: The property type is eligible and every applicable printed limit and condition holds.
There is no case for this outcome.

condition.purpose: Establish whether a Form 1007 is required and present for a DSCR transaction, or for a listed single-family transaction that meets a stated rent-schedule trigger.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal report and loan application for the transaction type, property type, and use of proposed rental income.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the transaction is a DSCR transaction; for a single-family property, determine whether it is a lease-option purchase with the required down payment generated from excess monthly rent contributions, or whether proposed rental income is being used to qualify.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify that the appraisal file contains a Form 1007 when required. For a single-family property, verify that the Form 1007 is from the original appraiser or a state licensed appraiser.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the required Form 1007 is present and, when applicable, from an acceptable appraiser.
checks: A Form 1007 is present for every DSCR transaction, including a No Ratio DSCR transaction.
For a single-family property that meets a stated single-family rent-schedule trigger, a Form 1007 is present.
A Form 1007 used for a single-family property is from the original appraiser or a state licensed appraiser.

outcomes.criterion: Every applicable check holds.
There is no case for this outcome.
An applicable check does not hold.

STD-1.7 “A 1007 will always be required on DSCR transactions – for avoidance of doubt, even on No Ratio DSCR”. Whether a Form 1025 satisfies this for a 2-4 unit property: Acra confirmation requested → Q-08. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-1.8 All borrowers purchasing or refinancing a one- to four-family investment property must execute a One- to Four-Family Rider with the loan documents and provide rent loss insurance coverage per §23.40 (STD-8.11 to 8.14). \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether required entity documentation is complete and meets the stated conditions.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the entity documents, identification, and any letter of explanation for a name discrepancy.
Eligibility Verification: Confirm the entity documents identify the entity and the persons authorized to sign and bind it.

Validation and Verification: Verify that a Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent is valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date; obtain qualification to operate in the relevant state if the entity was formed in another state; verify an IRS Form SS4, Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter, or an Acra Legal Department-reviewed EIN exception request with a letter of explanation; and verify a Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and identifying the authorized loan-document signor. Do not treat that consent as authorizing a personal-guarantee signor. Verify that any Power of Attorney used to execute a personal guarantee is utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact.

Final Determination: Record whether the required documentation is verified; note that Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

rule.description: Verify the entity documentation and authorization requirements stated for an entity borrower.

ledger.clause:
- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

rule.description: Verify that title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust meets every stated trust requirement.

ledger.clause:
STD-6.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the loan meets applicable DSCR-dependent requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan file for DSCR qualification method, LTV, CLTV, loan amount, property type, reserves, and other applicable features.
Eligibility Verification: Determine whether DSCR is calculated or No Ratio applies, and identify each ratio-dependent condition that applies.

Validation and Verification: If LTV > 80.00%, verify minimum DSCR 1.20 and 6 months PITIA reserves, and that the property is limited to SFR, Warrantable Condos outside of Florida, Townhome, PUD. If DSCR < 1.0 or No Ratio, apply maximum CLTV 75% purchase, 70% refinance — rate & term, 65% refinance — cash-out and minimum FICO 640. Apply the stated minimum DSCRs for applicable situations: loan amount over $2,000,000, 1.0; rural / unique property, 1.00; Non-Warrantable Condo or condotel / PUDtel, 1.0; first-time homebuyer, 1.150; vacant property rate & term refinance, 1.000; vacant property cash-out refinance, 1.15; property listed for sale within six months, 1.0; mixed use, adult care or assisted living, 1.2.
Final Determination: Record each applicable ratio-dependent threshold and whether it is met.
checks: If LTV > 80.00%, DSCR is at least 1.20, PITIA reserves are at least 6 months, and the property is within the listed eligible types.
If DSCR < 1.0 or No Ratio, CLTV does not exceed the purpose-specific cap and FICO is at least 640.
For each applicable situation listed in the validation step, DSCR meets its stated minimum.

ledger.clause:
STD-6.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

condition.purpose: Verify whether title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust meets STD-6.13.
steps: Initial Document Review: Obtain and review a complete, legible copy of the Trust or a Certification of Trust and the supporting trust and exception documents.
Eligibility Verification: Confirm whether title is to be vested in an inter vivos revocable trust.

Validation and Verification: Verify that the Trust or Certification of Trust states the existence and date of the Trust; Trustor(s) and current Trustee(s); Trustee powers; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of Trustees required to sign; the Trust identification number; how title to Trust assets should be taken; and that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner. Verify the Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established; is revocable and changeable or cancelable at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime; is established by one or more natural persons and effective during their lifetime; has the establishing individual(s) as primary beneficiary; and, if Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same, has written exception by Acra Senior Management. Note that Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.
Final Determination: Record whether every applicable trust requirement is met.

rule.description: Verify each stated requirement for title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust.

ledger.clause:
STD-6.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

STD-4.9 “Acra defines a First Time Home Buyers (‘FTHB’) as an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property).” \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.10 DSCR: Acra allows first-time homebuyers under all of the following: minimum 700 FICO score; maximum 70% CLTV; minimum DSCR of 1.150; maximum loan amount of \$1,000,000; full amortization required, no interest-only programs; impounds required; minimum six months reserves. The Summary states the same conditions: “Minimum 700 FICO: Max 70% CLTV: DSCR ≥ 1.15: Loan amt ≤ \$1MM: NO I/O: Must Impound: Requires 6mos Reserves”. \[G §3.13, p. 10; S: Restrictions\]

STD-4.11 “Where a FTHB is purchasing an Investment property and the loan is qualifying via DTI program, the maximum DTI will be 43.0%.” Noted as a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.12 §3.12 separately requires at least one guarantor with prior homeownership experience where the borrower is an entity (STD-6.9). How that requirement and the first-time-homebuyer allowance interact: Acra confirmation requested → Q-09.

condition.purpose: Determine the calculated DSCR for a file qualifying by calculated DSCR.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal_report and lease_agreement for market rent and annual in-place rent information; review the loan file for annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, homeowner's / condominium association fees, and subordinate financing, if applicable.

Final Determination: Divide the numerator by the denominator and record the calculated DSCR. Use the first payment due under the terms of the Note.

STD-3.1 “Acra calculates the DSCR by dividing (a) the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent (reference §14.14) by (b) the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (collectively, ‘PITIA’). Subordinate financing, if applicable, would also be included in the denominator for the sake of this calculation.” \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.2 “Acra calculates the DSCR utilizing the first payment due under the terms of the Note.” §7.5 defines Interest Only payments as “the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest to the mortgage on a monthly basis at the time of origination”, while the §5.32 denominator lists “annual principal, interest …”. Which payment enters the DSCR denominator on an interest-only loan: Acra confirmation requested → Q-26. \[G §7.5, p. 13; §5.32, p. 3\]

condition.purpose: Determine and name the case fact “Rent Loss Insurance Requirement Applies” for use by later jobs.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan application for the loan purpose and the case fields for the subject property's unit count and occupancy subtype.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the property is a one- to four-unit non-owner occupied income property and whether subject property rents are used to qualify; include No Ratio DSCR as stated in STD-8.12 and STD-3.22.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Apply the stated CLTV exemption of ≤ 70% and, where it does not resolve applicability, verify whether LTV is > 70%. If LTV is at or below 70% and CLTV is above 70%, obtain Acra confirmation (Q-11).
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether Rent Loss Insurance Requirement Applies, does not apply, or remains unresolved pending the stated Acra confirmation.
checks: SubjectProperty.number_of_units is 1, 2, 3, or 4.
SubjectProperty.occupancy_subtype is non-owner occupied.
LoanCore.loan_purpose is purchase or refinance of an investment property.

condition.purpose: Calculate DSCR as specified for the loan, using the first payment due under the terms of the Note.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Obtain annual in-place rent, market rent under §14.14, the first payment due under the terms of the Note, annual real estate taxes, property insurance, homeowner's / condominium association fees, and any applicable subordinate financing amount.

rule.description: Calculate DSCR using the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent divided by annual PITIA, including subordinate financing in the denominator if applicable.

ledger.clause:
STD-3.1 “Acra calculates the DSCR by dividing (a) the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent (reference §14.14) by (b) the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (collectively, ‘PITIA’). Subordinate financing, if applicable, would also be included in the denominator for the sake of this calculation.” \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.2 “Acra calculates the DSCR utilizing the first payment due under the terms of the Note.” §7.5 defines Interest Only payments as “the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest to the mortgage on a monthly basis at the time of origination”, while the §5.32 denominator lists “annual principal, interest …”. Which payment enters the DSCR denominator on an interest-only loan: Acra confirmation requested → Q-26. \[G §7.5, p. 13; §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.3 The reference to subordinate financing in the denominator is a calculation rule; it does not itself establish that a subordinate lien is permitted. Whether and when subordinate financing is permitted: Acra confirmation requested → Q-18. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.4 §14.14 (market rent), referenced in the formula, is not reproduced in the excerpt (Appendix B). \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-8.9 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI (Q-14); a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

STD-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (STD-9.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

STD-1.4 The matrix columns are Purchase, Rate & Term and Cash-Out. Delayed financing is addressed only by the matrix footnote “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”. rule.description: Verify the entity-borrower requirements for entity type, entity documentation, title ownership, guarantees, and guarantor homeownership experience.

ledger.clause:
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

STD-6.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-22. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

STD-6.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. See Q-09. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

rule.description: Determine whether the subject property meets the program's investment-property occupancy requirement.

ledger.clause:
The Standard DSCR program finances loans on investment property, qualified on the subject property's rent rather than the borrower's income; whether every loan is a business-purpose transaction is Q-27. This section collects the program-level requirements that apply before any matrix or overlay is consulted.

STD-1.1 Occupancy is investment property (non-owner occupied) only. \[S: Occupancy Type\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether required entity documentation is provided without relying on borrower letters stating documents are not required, available, or excused.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review entity formation, governance, ownership, qualification, tax identification, consent, and other supporting documents.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Identify which requirements apply to the entity type and circumstances, including corporation, LLC, partnership, formation state, and ownership documentation circumstances.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify each applicable requirement in the checks, including required contents, signatures, matching names, and timing. Do not accept a borrower letter stating required documents are not required, available, or excused.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the applicable required entity documents are provided and meet the stated requirements.
checks: A complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation or Articles of Organization and all amendments is provided.

For LLCs and Partnerships, a complete, legible Operating Agreement with all referenced exhibits and amendments is provided; for corporations, complete, legible Bylaws with all referenced exhibits and amendments are provided.

The applicable Operating Agreement or Bylaws states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers.
Where formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict, additional information required to address the conflict is provided.
Documentation evidencing all ownership interests is provided.

For LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement identifies by name all persons and their ownership interests, or copies of membership interest certificates or units in compliance with the Operating Agreement are provided.

For S or C Corporations, compliant shareholder or stockholder certificates are provided, if any, or the corporation's stock ledger is provided if stock certificates are lost or unavailable; the certificate or ledger accounts for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation or Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation.
If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is provided.

For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest and a CPA or Tax Preparer letter affirming current ownership interest are provided; if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed, the letter includes a statement to that effect.
Names on entity documents match the identification, or a letter of explanation addresses any discrepancy.
A Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date is provided.

If the entity is formed in a state other than where business is conducted or the property is located, a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the applicable state is provided.

An IRS Form SS4, Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity is provided, unless an EIN exception request is submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

A Unanimous Written Consent or Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest authorizes the transaction with Acra Lending and identifies who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity.
A Unanimous Written Consent or Board Resolution is not used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee.
A Power of Attorney is utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee when required by the stated requirement.
Any additional supporting documentation conditioned by Legal in its sole discretion is provided.

outcomes.criterion: Every applicable required entity document is provided and meets the stated requirements; no borrower letter is used to claim that a required document is not required, available, or excused.

An EIN exception request is submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds, or Legal has conditioned the file for additional supporting documentation that remains to be provided.
An applicable required document or required information is missing or deficient, or a borrower letter is relied on to claim a required document is not required, available, or excused.
The borrower is not an entity borrower.

Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

ledger.clause:
STD-6.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

PLAT-1.7 The program is offered through two channels with different minimum ratios: Correspondent ≥ 1.2, Wholesale ≥ 1.0 (PLAT-3.7). Matrix footnote 3 also restricts Correspondent pricing (PLAT-2.3). \[P: Minimum DSCR; matrix footnote 3\]

PLAT-1.8 Every loan must meet the applicable channel minimum DSCR. The Platinum Summary lists no No Ratio option and no allowance for a ratio below 1.0; a ratio below the channel minimum does not meet the published requirement. Whether No Ratio or sub-1.0 qualification exists on this program in any form: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[P: Minimum DSCR\]

PLAT-1.9 Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. PLAT-1.10 “A 1007 will always be required on DSCR transactions”; the Platinum Summary refers to market rent “as established on the 1007 or 1025”. Whether a Form 1025 alone satisfies the requirement for a two-unit property: Acra confirmation requested → Q-04. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.12, p. 4; P: Income Documentation\]

PLAT-1.11 All borrowers purchasing or refinancing a one- to four-family investment property must execute a One- to Four-Family Rider with the loan documents and provide rent loss insurance coverage per §23.40 (PLAT-7.9 to 7.12). \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

PLAT-1.12 Only the subject property, principal residence and second homes are required to be listed on the application or Schedule of Real Estate Owned. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §4.15, p. 5\]

A 1007 may be from the original appraiser or any state licensed appraiser. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

PLAT-3.10 Single family investment properties with excessive monthly rent payments reflected on the lease require documentation supporting that the monthly rent is typical for the area; acceptable documentation may include classified ads from local newspapers, a 1007 completed by the appraiser, or a market rent survey completed by a local real estate company or rental management company familiar with the market rents in the area. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-18. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

Eligibility Verification: Verify that the operating agreement or bylaws includes all referenced exhibits, states whether the entity is member or manager managed, authorizes borrowing money and entering into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers; verify that ownership interests are evidenced as required for the entity type.

Validation and Verification: Verify that entity names match identification or that a letter of explanation addresses a discrepancy; verify a Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date; and review any applicable foreign qualification, IRS Form SS4 or TIN/EIN issuance letter, unanimous written consent or board resolution, and power of attorney.

Final Determination: Record whether all applicable required documents and stated contents are present. Do not accept a borrower letter stating that required documents are not required, available, or excused.
checks: The complete, legible formation document and all amendments are provided.
The applicable complete, legible operating agreement or bylaws and all amendments satisfy the stated content requirements.
All required ownership-interest documentation for the entity type is provided.
Names on the entity documents match identification, or a letter of explanation addresses any discrepancy.
A Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent is valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.
Where applicable, the entity has provided qualification to operate in the relevant state and an IRS Form SS4 or TIN/EIN issuance letter.
A unanimous written consent or board resolution signed by all members authorizes the transaction and identifies an authorized signer for the entity's loan documents.
Where a power of attorney is used to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee, the required power of attorney is provided.

rule.description: Verify that the required entity documents are complete and satisfy the stated content and timing requirements.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-5.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

rule.description: Verify that each required entity-borrower guarantor requirement is met.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-18. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

citations: Acra_DSCR_Platinum_Select_Consolidated_Guidelines_v1_0 1.docx#8.1 Gift funds, funds to close and seasoning

ledger.clause:
PLAT-8.1 Gift funds, investment property: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price (PLAT-1.15). \[G §8.7, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction is Q-22. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing”. Foreign nationals are not eligible for this program, but an eligible US citizen or permanent resident may hold funds abroad; the same sentence's 60-day seasoning requirement is stated for Foreign Nationals only and is not restated. Whether the repatriation requirement applies to eligible borrowers holding funds abroad, and what evidence and timing convention apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.6 “See guidelines for unacceptable source of funds” — the Seller's Guide provision is not reproduced (Appendix B). \[P: Reserve Requirements\]

ledger.clause:
PLAT-5.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

One matrix covers all loan amounts to \$2,000,000. It is reproduced below exactly as printed, followed by its footnotes in Acra's words. The printed FICO thresholds are 730, 721 and 700, which leaves a score of exactly 720 to be read literally; the reading and its consequences are set out for Acra to confirm rather than adopted. PLAT-2.1 The rows below are Acra's. Each row is a minimum-FICO threshold: a score at or above the threshold and below the next higher threshold takes that row. No row is printed below 700. \[P: Loan Amount, FICO, CLTV Requirements\] | **Min FICO** | **Purchase** | **Rate & Term** | **Cash-Out** | |--------------|--------------|-----------------|--------------| | 730 | 80% | 80% | 75% | | 721 | 80% | 80% | 65% | | 700 | 80% | 80% | 55% |

Read literally, a decisioning score of 720 falls in the 700 row (cash-out maximum 55%), sits outside the Correspondent restriction printed for “700-719 FICO” (footnote 3), and takes the 3.25 ARM margin printed for “720-759”. This document does not normalize 721 to 720. Whether the 721 threshold is intended, and how 720 is treated on each of the three points: Acra confirmation requested → Q-01.

ledger.clause:
The Platinum Summary lists two eligible citizenship types and excludes first-time homebuyers. Borrowing entities, guarantors and trusts follow the Seller's Guide excerpt and are in section 5.

PLAT-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.3 Non-permanent residents, foreign nationals and ITIN borrowers are not among the listed eligible types. The Seller's Guide foreign-national program (§3.10) is therefore not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.4 “First Time Homebuyer (FTHB) ineligible for this program”. Acra defines a First Time Home Buyer as “an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property)”; the §3.13 DSCR allowance for first-time homebuyers is not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements; G §3.13, p. 10\]

PLAT-4.5 §3.12 requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience, and at least one borrower / guarantor to attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer (PLAT-5.9). Whether it applies to individual borrowers as well as entities is part of Q-13. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

condition.purpose: Verify the entity documents required by PLAT-5.10 and the related requirements in the Seller’s Guide excerpt.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the entity documents and all applicable amendments, exhibits, ownership records, certificates, resolutions, and supporting documents.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Identify the entity type and determine which entity-specific documentation requirements apply.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify each applicable check against the entity documents. Borrower letters stating that required documents are not required, available, or excused do not satisfy the requirements.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the applicable required documentation is complete. Note any additional supporting documentation conditioned for by Legal.
checks: A complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation or Articles of Organization and all amendments is present.

For an LLC or Partnership, a complete, legible Operating Agreement with all referenced exhibits and amendments is present; for a corporation, a complete, legible set of Bylaws with all referenced exhibits and amendments is present; the applicable document states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers.

Documentation evidencing all ownership interests is present: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement identifies or attaches all persons by name with their ownership interest, or membership interest certificates or units are provided in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

For an S or C Corporation, shareholder or stockholder certificates complying with the Bylaws, if any, or the corporation’s stock ledger when certificates are lost or unavailable, accounts for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation or Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation; an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is present when stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable.

For an S-corporation or Partnership where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, the most recent preceding tax year’s K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest and a CPA or Tax Preparer letter affirming current ownership interest are present; if the preceding year’s taxes have not been filed, the letter includes a statement to that effect.
Names on the entity documents match the identification, or a letter of explanation addresses any discrepancy where the names do not match exactly.
A Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date is present.

If the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located, a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted is present.

An IRS Form SS4, Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity is present; if an EIN exception request is submitted, it includes a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds for review by Acra’s Legal Department.

A Unanimous Written Consent or Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest authorizes the transaction with Acra Lending and identifies who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity.
If a principal designates an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee, a Power of Attorney is utilized by the principal.
A borrower letter stating that a required document is not required, available, or excused from providing is not used as a substitute for that required document.

outcomes.criterion: Every applicable check holds and no additional supporting documentation conditioned for by Legal remains outstanding.
Every applicable check holds, but additional supporting documentation conditioned for by Legal remains outstanding.
An applicable required-document check does not hold.
The borrower is not an entity borrower.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-5.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

PLAT-3.1 “When calculating the DSCR, Acra will use the greater of the market rent as established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent. When using actual rent, the actual rent must be documented via evidence of 2 months’ proof of receipts and the lease must be in place for at least 3 months after the loan closing. This applies to long-term rents only and is not appropriate for short-term rentals.” \[P: Income Documentation & Debt Ratio Requirements\]

PLAT-3.2 §5.32 of the excerpt states the general formula as “the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent”, then notes that “Acra may use the higher of actual or market rents” subject to “two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt”, a lease continuing at least three months after closing, and: “Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” The Platinum Summary's statement (PLAT-3.1) is program-specific; the excerpt's general formula is reproduced here. condition.purpose: Determine whether an entity borrower meets the published entity eligibility requirements.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review entity documents for entity type, formation and base, ownership, purpose, and any nesting or ownership changes.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Verify that the entity type is allowed; it is US formed and based; it meets the single purpose entity requirement where applicable; and it is not a prohibited entity type or structure.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify that every entity holding direct ownership of the subject property is a borrowing entity; that direct or indirect owners with ≥ 20% provide a recourse guarantee; and that ownership changes made to circumvent required guarantees are not recognized when made within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the entity borrower and its ownership and guarantee structure meet the requirements.
checks: The entity type and ownership structure are allowed by the program.
The entity is US formed and based, and an entity borrower meets the stated SPE requirements.
Every entity holding direct ownership of the subject property is a borrowing entity.
Each individual with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% provides a recourse guarantee.
No ownership change made to circumvent required personal guarantors is relied on if it occurred within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process.

outcomes.criterion: Every entity eligibility, ownership, and guarantee check holds.
Required entity documents or recourse guarantees remain to be provided or verified.
An entity eligibility, ownership, or guarantee check does not hold.
The borrower is not an entity borrower.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-18. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the representative credit score and CLTV meet the published matrix requirements.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the credit report and loan application for the representative score, loan purpose, and CLTV.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Verify that the representative score is at least 700 and select the matrix row: 730 and above; 721 to 729; or 700 to 720.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Compare CLTV with the matrix maximum for the loan purpose and selected row: Purchase 80% in each row; Rate & Term 80% in each row; Cash-Out 75% at 730 and above, 65% at 721 to 729, and 55% at 700 to 720. For Correspondent loans with a score of 700-719, verify the stated 60% CLTV pricing limit; the cash-out matrix maximum remains 55% where applicable.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the minimum score and applicable matrix CLTV requirements are met.
checks: The representative score is at least 700.
The CLTV does not exceed the matrix maximum for the loan purpose and representative-score row.
For a Correspondent loan with a score of 700-719, the CLTV does not exceed 60%.

outcomes.criterion: Every applicable score and CLTV check holds.
There is no case for this outcome.
The representative score is below 700 or an applicable CLTV check does not hold.
There is no case for this outcome.

ledger.clause:
One matrix covers all loan amounts to \$2,000,000. It is reproduced below exactly as printed, followed by its footnotes in Acra's words. The printed FICO thresholds are 730, 721 and 700, which leaves a score of exactly 720 to be read literally; the reading and its consequences are set out for Acra to confirm rather than adopted. PLAT-2.1 The rows below are Acra's. Each row is a minimum-FICO threshold: a score at or above the threshold and below the next higher threshold takes that row. No row is printed below 700. \[P: Loan Amount, FICO, CLTV Requirements\] | **Min FICO** | **Purchase** | **Rate & Term** | **Cash-Out** | |--------------|--------------|-----------------|--------------| | 730 | 80% | 80% | 75% | | 721 | 80% | 80% | 65% | | 700 | 80% | 80% | 55% |

THE PRINTED 721 THRESHOLD AND A SCORE OF 720

Read literally, a decisioning score of 720 falls in the 700 row (cash-out maximum 55%), sits outside the Correspondent restriction printed for “700-719 FICO” (footnote 3), and takes the 3.25 ARM margin printed for “720-759”. This document does not normalize 721 to 720. Whether the 721 threshold is intended, and how 720 is treated on each of the three points: Acra confirmation requested → Q-01.
PLAT-2.2 Footnote 1, whose marker is printed on the Cash-Out column heading: “When LTV \> 65% Max Cash-in-Hand: \$1,000,000 for loans ≥ \$1,500,000, \$500,000 for loans \< \$1,500,000.” Footnote 2, whose marker appears nowhere in the matrix: “When LTV ≤ 65%, unlimited cash-in-hand allowed.” The footnotes are stated in LTV while the matrix is labelled CLTV: Acra confirmation requested → Q-16. \[P: matrix footnotes 1–2\] PLAT-2.3 Footnote 3, whose marker also appears nowhere in the matrix: “Correspondent Pricing limited to 60% CLTV for 700-719 FICO”. For a Correspondent cash-out at 700-719 the matrix already prints 55%; the 60% footnote does not raise that figure. How the two limits apply together by purpose: Acra confirmation requested → Q-01. \[P: matrix footnote 3\] PLAT-2.4 Footnote \*: “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM” (PLAT-1.4, Q-02). \[P: matrix footnote\]

ledger.clause:
The Platinum Summary lists two eligible citizenship types and excludes first-time homebuyers. Borrowing entities, guarantors and trusts follow the Seller's Guide excerpt and are in section 5.

PLAT-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.3 Non-permanent residents, foreign nationals and ITIN borrowers are not among the listed eligible types. The Seller's Guide foreign-national program (§3.10) is therefore not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.4 “First Time Homebuyer (FTHB) ineligible for this program”. Acra defines a First Time Home Buyer as “an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property)”; the §3.13 DSCR allowance for first-time homebuyers is not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements; G §3.13, p. 10\]

PLAT-4.5 §3.12 requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience, and at least one borrower / guarantor to attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer (PLAT-5.9). Whether it applies to individual borrowers as well as entities is part of Q-13. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

Each exclusion below follows from an express statement in the Platinum Summary, quoted in the middle column. Acra is asked to confirm each (Q-13, Q-20). Provisions the Summary neither excludes nor addresses are listed separately in B.2 and are asked, not excluded.

| §3.13 First Time Home Buyer — DSCR conditions | “First Time Homebuyer (FTHB) ineligible for this program” | Definition kept at PLAT-4.4; conditions not restated |

ledger.clause:
PLAT-3.4 Denominator, per §5.32: “the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (collectively, ‘PITIA’). Subordinate financing, if applicable, would also be included in the denominator for the sake of this calculation.” \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.5 “Acra calculates the DSCR utilizing the first payment due under the terms of the Note.” §7.5 defines Interest Only payments as “the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest to the mortgage on a monthly basis at the time of origination”, while the §5.32 denominator lists “annual principal, interest …”. Which payment enters the DSCR denominator on an interest-only loan: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. \[G §7.5, p. 13; §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.6 The reference to subordinate financing in the denominator is a calculation rule; it does not itself establish that a subordinate lien is permitted. The Platinum Summary does not address subordinate financing or restate the Standard Summary's HELOC calculation: Acra confirmation requested → Q-15. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the required Business Purpose Attestation or an Acra-approved similar attestation is executed with the loan documents when the stated applicability conditions hold.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application for the transaction purpose and qualification basis, and review the loan documents for an executed attestation.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Establish whether the borrower qualifies utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: If those applicability conditions hold, verify that the borrower executed with the loan documents a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.

Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the attestation requirement is met when applicable. The source requests Acra confirmation on whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction; do not assume universal applicability.
checks: When the borrower qualifies utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, the borrower executed with the loan documents a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.

condition.purpose: Determine whether a Delayed Financing loan is within the stated $1.5MM cap.

steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review entity_documents and the loan_application for the entity type, formation and base, ownership structure, entity purpose, and subject-property use.
