PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-18. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the required entity documents and stated contents are provided.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review entity_documents and identification for a complete, legible Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments; the applicable complete, legible Operating Agreement or Bylaws and all amendments; ownership-interest evidence; and all other documents listed in these steps. Borrower letters stating that required documents are not required, available, or excused are not acceptable.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Verify that the Operating Agreement or Bylaws states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. If formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict, note that additional information may be required. Verify that ownership-interest evidence accounts for the owners as specified in the source.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: For S or C Corporations, verify shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or the corporation's stock ledger if certificates are lost or unavailable; it must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, verify an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate. For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, verify the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest and a CPA or Tax Preparer letter affirming current ownership interest; if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed, verify a statement to that effect. Verify that entity-document names match identification or that a letter of explanation addresses any discrepancy; a Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent is valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date; a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is conducted is provided if the entity was formed in another state; and IRS Form SS4 or an EIN/TIN issuance letter is provided. EIN exception requests may be submitted to Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds. Verify a Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot designate a signor on a personal guarantee. A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced. Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether all documents applicable to the entity type and circumstances are present, complete, legible, and contain the required information. Do not accept borrower letters as substitutes for required documents.
checks: A complete, legible Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments is provided.

The applicable complete, legible Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments are provided, with required management, borrowing, contract, and signer provisions.
The ownership-interest evidence required for the entity type is provided and accounts for the relevant ownership interests.
Applicable corporate share certificates or stock ledger meet the stated requirements, and an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is provided when required.

When both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable for an S-corporation or Partnership, the required K-1 statements and CPA or Tax Preparer letter are provided, including the statement about unfiled preceding-year taxes when applicable.
Entity-document names match identification, or a letter of explanation addresses discrepancies.
A Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent is valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.
A Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is conducted is provided when the entity was formed in another state.

condition.purpose: Determine whether title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust meets the stated requirements.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review entity_documents for a complete, legible copy of the Trust or a Certification of Trust. The Certification must state the existence and date of the Trust; Trustor(s) and current Trustee(s); Trustee powers; whether the Trust is revocable and, if so, who holds the right to revoke; the number and names of Trustees required to sign; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to Trust assets should be taken; and that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Verify that the Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established; is revocable and can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime; is established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly, and becomes effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it; and has as its primary beneficiary the individual(s) establishing it.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: If the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same, verify that written exception by Acra Senior Management has been obtained. Verify that the Trust specifies the Trustee's power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary need not grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor. Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether every applicable trust-title requirement is met. Irrevocable trusts are not permitted.
checks: A complete, legible Trust or Certification of Trust containing all stated required information is provided.
The Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established and is revocable, with the stated lifetime power to change or cancel it.
The Trust is established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly, and becomes effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.
The primary beneficiary of the Trust is the individual(s) establishing it.

rule.description: Verify the stated conditions for title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-5.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

rule.description: Python formalization of acra-standard.asset_assessment.first_time_homebuyer_reserves

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Verify the minimum six months reserves requirement for a first-time homebuyer.
PURPOSE: Determine whether the reserve requirement for a first-time homebuyer is met.
CHECKS (encode those the case fields settle; leave the rest to a reviewer):
  - A first-time homebuyer has minimum six months reserves.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-4.9 “Acra defines a First Time Home Buyers (‘FTHB’) as an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property).” \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.10 DSCR: Acra allows first-time homebuyers under all of the following: minimum 700 FICO score; maximum 70% CLTV; minimum DSCR of 1.150; maximum loan amount of \$1,000,000; full amortization required, no interest-only programs; impounds required; minimum six months reserves. The Summary states the same conditions: “Minimum 700 FICO: Max 70% CLTV: DSCR ≥ 1.15: Loan amt ≤ \$1MM: NO I/O: Must Impound: Requires 6mos Reserves”. \[G §3.13, p. 10; S: Restrictions\]

STD-4.11 “Where a FTHB is purchasing an Investment property and the loan is qualifying via DTI program, the maximum DTI will be 43.0%.” Noted as a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.12 §3.12 separately requires at least one guarantor with prior homeownership experience where the borrower is an entity (STD-6.9). How that requirement and the first-time-homebuyer allowance interact: Acra confirmation requested → Q-09.

STD-9.6 The sources state reserves only for the situations below, and state the payment basis only where shown. The base requirement where no trigger applies, the payment basis where only “months” is stated, permitted sources, whether overlapping triggers are cumulative, and whether reserves substituted for rent loss insurance are additional: Acra confirmation requested → Q-07. \[S; G\]

| **Trigger** | **Reserves as printed** | **Source** |
|----|----|----|
| LTV \> 80.00% | 6 months PITIA reserves | S: Income Documentation |
| FICO \< 620 | 12 Months | S: Credit Requirements |
| First-time homebuyer | Minimum six months reserves (“Requires 6mos Reserves”) | G §3.13; S: Restrictions |
| Vacant property — rate & term refinance | Minimum six months reserves | G §10.17; S: Occupancy Type |
| Vacant property — cash-out refinance | 6 months reserves | S: Occupancy Type |
| Property listed for sale within six months | Twenty-four (24) months of reserves; cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide | G §11.5 |
| Forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, tenant-occupied subject, without timely receipt of the prior two months' rent | 12 months of the subject's payment in reserve, which may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand | G §5.32 |
| Rent loss insurance required but cannot be obtained | Two (2) months reserves for every one (1) month of coverage not provided | G §23.40 |

proposals.reasoning: The stated first-time-homebuyer requirement is a minimum of six months reserves, so six meets the requirement and fewer than six does not. When the borrower is not a first-time homebuyer, this specific check does not apply. Other reserve triggers and requirements are left to a reviewer.

rule.description: Python formalization of acra-standard.asset_assessment.foreign_national_funds_seasoning_and_repatriation
citations: Acra_DSCR_Standard_Consolidated_Guidelines_v1_0.docx#9.1 Gift funds, funds to close and seasoning

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Verify the minimum seasoning and repatriation requirements for Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV.
PURPOSE: Determine whether a Foreign National's funds meet the stated seasoning and repatriation requirements.
CHECKS (encode those the case fields settle; leave the rest to a reviewer):
  - A Foreign National documents a minimum of 60 days seasoning, regardless of LTV / CLTV.
  - Funds held in a foreign bank / currency are repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-5.6 Assets held / foreign accounts must be verified in U.S. Dollar equivalency at the current exchange rate via www.xe.com or the Wall Street Journal conversion table. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.7 Sufficient funds to close must be on deposit with the Escrow / Closing Agent at least three (3) business days (including Saturdays for this calculation) prior to any closing date. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.8 A copy of the two (2) most recent statements of that account is required. If the funds are not seasoned a minimum of sixty (60) days, a letter of explanation is required along with the information to comprise a sixty (60) day chain of funds. Bank statements in any language other than English must be translated into English. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.9 Per §8.4, Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning, and funds held in a foreign bank / currency must be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing (STD-9.5). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.1 Gift funds, investment property or second homes: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B). \[G §8.7, p. 12; S: Loan Amount\]

STD-9.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing and Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning.” Whether the repatriation requirement applies to any borrower holding funds abroad or only to foreign nationals, and what evidence applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

proposals.reasoning: The allowed case fields do not include evidence of seasoning duration, whether funds are held in a foreign bank/currency, or repatriation and closing dates. Therefore, for a Foreign National, the stated 60-day and three-business-day requirements cannot be evaluated and are left undecided for a reviewer. No threshold-side test cases can be made from the permitted fields; the case shown verifies only that the requirements do not apply to a stated non-Foreign National.

condition.source:
import rules_lib

def check(ctx):
    representative_score = ctx['CreditReport.representative_score']
    cltv_percent = ctx['LoanCore.cltv_percent']
    total_loan_amount_usd = ctx['LoanCore.total_loan_amount_usd']
    is_interest_only = rules_lib.flag(ctx['MortgageLoanInformation.is_interest_only'])
    is_escrow_waived = rules_lib.flag(ctx['LoanCore.is_escrow_waived'])
    reserves_months = ctx['RatioSet.reserves_months']

    missing = rules_lib.gaps(
        representative_score=representative_score,
        cltv_percent=cltv_percent,
        total_loan_amount_usd=total_loan_amount_usd,
        is_interest_only=is_interest_only,
        is_escrow_waived=is_escrow_waived,
        reserves_months=reserves_months,
    )
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    return (
        representative_score >= 700
        and cltv_percent <= 70
        and total_loan_amount_usd <= 1000000
        and not is_interest_only
        and not is_escrow_waived
        and reserves_months >= 6
    )

condition.source:
def check(ctx):
    property_type = ctx['SubjectProperty.property_type']
    number_of_units = ctx['SubjectProperty.number_of_units']
    occupancy_subtype = ctx['SubjectProperty.occupancy_subtype']
    has_current_lease = rules_lib.flag(ctx['SubjectProperty.has_current_lease'])
    is_vacant = rules_lib.flag(ctx['SubjectProperty.is_vacant'])

    missing = rules_lib.gaps(
        property_type=property_type,
        number_of_units=number_of_units,
        occupancy_subtype=occupancy_subtype,
        has_current_lease=has_current_lease,
        is_vacant=is_vacant,
    )
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    eligible_type = rules_lib.same(
        property_type,
        'residential dwelling',
        'one-to-four-unit residential dwelling',
        'single family',
        'one family',
        '1-4 family',
        '2-4 family',
        'condominium',
        'condo',
        'PUD',
        'planned unit development',
    )
    investment_occupancy = rules_lib.same(
        occupancy_subtype, 'investment', 'investment property', 'non-owner occupied'
    )

    return bool(
        eligible_type
        and 1 <= number_of_units <= 4
        and investment_occupancy
        and has_current_lease
        and not is_vacant
    )

  - The property is a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD.
  - The owner does not occupy the dwelling.
  - The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.
  - A 1007 is provided on every DSCR transaction, including No Ratio DSCR.
  - Borrowers purchasing or refinancing a one- to four-family investment property execute a One- to Four-Family Rider with the loan documents and provide rent loss insurance coverage.
  - Where the borrower qualifies using the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, the borrower executes with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.
  - Only the subject property, principal residence, and second homes are required to be listed on the application or Schedule of Real Estate Owned.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-1.1 Occupancy is investment property (non-owner occupied) only. \[S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (STD-9.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

STD-1.4 The matrix columns are Purchase, Rate & Term and Cash-Out. Delayed financing is addressed only by the matrix footnote “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”. Which column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-06. \[S: matrix and footnote\]

STD-1.5 A loan qualifies either by a calculated DSCR (§5.32) or as No Ratio DSCR, where no ratio is calculated (§5.33). Both are set out in section 3. \[G §5.32–5.33, p. 3\]

STD-1.6 “Borrowing entity income documentation not required.” Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. \[S: Income Documentation; G §7.3, p. 5\]

STD-1.7 “A 1007 will always be required on DSCR transactions – for avoidance of doubt, even on No Ratio DSCR”. Whether a Form 1025 satisfies this for a 2-4 unit property: Acra confirmation requested → Q-08. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-1.8 All borrowers purchasing or refinancing a one- to four-family investment property must execute a One- to Four-Family Rider with the loan documents and provide rent loss insurance coverage per §23.40 (STD-8.11 to 8.14). \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-1.9 Only the subject property, principal residence and second homes are required to be listed on the application or Schedule of Real Estate Owned. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §4.15, p. 5\]

proposals.reasoning: Checks only the available property-type/unit-count and investment-occupancy/lease/vacancy fields. The source also requires year-round principal-residence occupancy by non-owner individuals, and specifies documents, insurance, and application/SREO listing requirements; the permitted case fields do not settle those matters, so they remain for reviewer verification.

def check(ctx):
    structure = ctx['LoanCore.prepayment_penalty_structure']
    missing = rules_lib.gaps(structure=structure)
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    printed_structures = (
        '5 Year 5% Fixed (5% / 5% / 5% / 5% / 5%)',
        '5 Year Sequential Stepdown (5% / 4% / 3% / 2% / 1%)',
        '4 Year 5% Fixed (5% / 5% / 5% / 5%)',
        '4 Year 3% Fixed (3% / 3% / 3% / 3%)',
        '3 Year 5% Fixed (5% / 5% / 5%)',
        '3 Year 3% Fixed (3% / 3% / 3%)',
        '2 Year 3% Fixed (3% / 3%)',
        '1 Year 3% Fixed (3%)',
        'No Prepay',
    )
    return any(rules_lib.same(structure, option) for option in printed_structures)

PURPOSE: Determine whether a property listed for sale within the defined period meets the stated eligibility characteristics.

CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER:

STD-8.8 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

condition.source:
import rules_lib

def check(ctx):
    property_type = ctx['SubjectProperty.property_type']
    state = ctx['SubjectProperty.state']
    missing = rules_lib.gaps(property_type=property_type, state=state)
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    eligible_types = (
        'SFR',
        'Townhome',
        'PUD',
        'Warrantable Condo',
        'Non-Warrantable Condo',
        'Condotel / PUDtel',
        '2-4 Units',
        'Manufactured',
    )
    return (
        any(rules_lib.same(property_type, item) for item in eligible_types)
        and not rules_lib.same(state, 'SD')
    )

  - Documentation evidencing ownership interests is provided in the form required for the entity type.

STD-6.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

proposals.reasoning: The available entity-documentation field settles only whether the entity documents are complete as a whole. The individual document, content, consistency, and timing requirements cannot be assessed from the permitted fields, so this function does not make separate determinations about them. An unstated or unrecognized completeness value is undecided.

PURPOSE: Verify the entity requirements in STD-6.3 through STD-6.6.

SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

Other listed checks require facts not present among the allowed fields (such as ownership percentages, guarantors, SPE assets and activity, direct owners on title, or agreement-change timing), so they are left to a reviewer. No numeric threshold is encoded because no allowed field supplies the ownership percentage.

import rules_lib

def check(ctx):
    loan_purpose = ctx['LoanCore.loan_purpose']
    occupancy_subtype = ctx['SubjectProperty.occupancy_subtype']
    entity_type = ctx['Borrower.entity_type']

    missing = rules_lib.gaps(
        loan_purpose=loan_purpose,
        occupancy_subtype=occupancy_subtype,
        entity_type=entity_type,
    )
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    business_purpose = rules_lib.same(
        loan_purpose,
        'business purpose',
        'business purpose transaction',
    )
    investment_property = rules_lib.same(
        occupancy_subtype,
        'investment',
        'investment property',
    )
    allowed_entity_type = rules_lib.same(
        entity_type,
        'domestic corporation',
        'domestic C corporation',
        'domestic S corporation',
        'C corporation',
        'S corporation',
        'C corp',
        'S corp',
        'single purpose LLC',
        'single purpose limited liability company',
        'LLC',
        'limited liability company',
        'LLP',
        'limited liability partnership',
        'LLLP',
        'limited liability limited partnership',
        'GP',
        'general partnership',
        'LP',
        'limited partnership',
        'sole proprietorship',
    )

    return business_purpose and investment_property and allowed_entity_type

condition.source:
import rules_lib


def check(ctx):
    citizenship = ctx['Borrower.citizenship_status']
    missing = rules_lib.gaps(citizenship=citizenship)
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)
    if not rules_lib.same(citizenship, 'Foreign National'):
        return True

    purpose = ctx['LoanCore.loan_purpose']
    score = ctx['CreditReport.representative_score']
    missing = rules_lib.gaps(purpose=purpose, representative_score=score)
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    is_purchase = rules_lib.same(purpose, 'purchase')
    is_rate_term = rules_lib.same(
        purpose,
        'rate & term',
        'rate and term',
        'rate term',
        'rate/term',
        'rate & term refinance',
        'rate and term refinance',
        'rate/term refinance',
        'refinance rate & term',
        'refinance rate and term',
    )
    is_cash_out = rules_lib.same(
        purpose,
        'cash-out',
        'cash out',
        'cash-out refinance',
        'cash out refinance',
        'refinance cash-out',
        'refinance cash out',
    )

    cltv = None
    if is_purchase or is_rate_term or is_cash_out:
        cltv = ctx['LoanCore.cltv_percent']
        missing = rules_lib.gaps(cltv=cltv)
        if missing:
            return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    if score != 700:
        return False
    if is_purchase:
        return cltv <= 70
    if is_rate_term or is_cash_out:
        return cltv <= 65
    return True

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Apply the stated DSCR, CLTV, FICO, and reserve requirements for loans with DSCR below 1.0, No Ratio DSCR, or LTV above 80.00%.

STD-3.16 LTV \> 80.00%: requires a minimum DSCR of 1.20 and 6 months PITIA reserves; limited to SFR, Warrantable Condos outside of Florida, Townhome, PUD. Stated in LTV where the matrix is labelled CLTV: Acra confirmation requested → Q-17. \[S: Income Documentation\]

STD-3.17 DSCR \< 1.0 or No Ratio: maximum CLTV 75% (purchase), 70% (refinance — rate & term), 65% (refinance — cash-out); minimum FICO 640. \[S: Income Documentation\]

| **Situation** | **Minimum DSCR as stated** | **Source** |
|----|----|----|
| LTV above 80.00% | 1.20 | S: Income Documentation |
| Loan amount over \$2,000,000 | 1.0 | S: Loan Amount |
| 1 or no score / deficient tradelines | 1.1 | S: Credit Requirements |
| Rural / unique property | 1.00 | S: Subject Property Location |
| Non-warrantable condo; condotel / PUDtel | 1.0 | S: Subject Property Type |
| First-time homebuyer | 1.150 | G §3.13; S: Restrictions |
| Vacant property, rate & term refinance | 1.000 (“OR Maximum 40.0% DTI” — Q-14) | G §10.17; S: Occupancy Type |
| Vacant property, cash-out refinance | 1.15 | S: Occupancy Type |
| Property listed for sale within six months | 1.0 (“or (b) 43% maximum DTI” — Q-14) | G §11.5 |
| Mixed use, adult care or assisted living | 1.2 | G §10.7 |

STD-3.19 “File can qualify without calculating a DSCR Ratio to a maximum LTV / CLTV as described on the appropriate program matrix depending on FICO and other requirement. Requires 1007; however, DSCR is not calculated.” The Summary's No Ratio caps and minimum FICO are STD-3.17. \[G §5.33, p. 3; S: Income Documentation\]

STD-3.20 “Proof of actual rents is not required. Property may be short-term rental or long-term rental (appropriate pricing applies).” \[G §5.33, p. 3\]

The source’s LTV/CLTV labeling discrepancy is noted in the code; CLTV is the only permitted field for this check. DSCR itself is not among the permitted fields, so for a non-No-Ratio method the below-1.0 trigger cannot be evaluated and the function returns an unknown verdict rather than assuming it is met or unmet. The reviewer-only DSCR-at-least-1.20 and reserve requirements are not enforced.

condition.source:
import rules_lib


def check(ctx):
    property_type = ctx['SubjectProperty.property_type']
    state = ctx['SubjectProperty.state']

    missing = rules_lib.gaps(property_type=property_type, state=state)
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    eligible_type = rules_lib.same(
        property_type,
        'SFR',
        'Townhome',
        'PUD',
        'Warrantable Condo',
        'Non-Warrantable Condo',
        'Condotel / PUDtel',
        '2-4 Units',
        'Manufactured',
    )
    eligible_state = not rules_lib.same(state, 'SD')
    return eligible_type and eligible_state

rule.description: Python formalization of acra-standard.loan_program_eligibility.eligible_subject_property

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Verify that the subject property's type and location meet the program-level eligibility requirements.
PURPOSE: Determine whether the subject property type is eligible and whether its state is ineligible.
CHECKS TO ENCODE:
  - SubjectProperty.property_type is one of SFR, Townhome, PUD, Warrantable Condo, Non-Warrantable Condo, Condotel / PUDtel, 2-4 Units, or Manufactured.
  - SubjectProperty.state is not SD.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-1.1 Occupancy is investment property (non-owner occupied) only. \[S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (STD-9.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

STD-1.4 The matrix columns are Purchase, Rate & Term and Cash-Out. Delayed financing is addressed only by the matrix footnote “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”. Which column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-06. \[S: matrix and footnote\]

STD-1.5 A loan qualifies either by a calculated DSCR (§5.32) or as No Ratio DSCR, where no ratio is calculated (§5.33). Both are set out in section 3. \[G §5.32–5.33, p. 3\]

STD-1.6 “Borrowing entity income documentation not required.” Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. \[S: Income Documentation; G §7.3, p. 5\]

STD-1.13 Ineligible state: SD. \[S: Subject Property Location\]

STD-1.14 Declining market: “-5% CLTV property/borrower full profile”. How this reduction combines with other caps: Acra confirmation requested → Q-07. \[S: Subject Property Location\]

STD-8.1 Eligible property types: SFR, Townhome, PUD, Warrantable Condo, Non-Warrantable Condo, Condotel / PUDtel, 2-4 Units, Manufactured. Restrictions as printed: \[S: Subject Property Type\]

| **Property type** | **Purchase** | **Refi R/T** | **Refi C/O** | **Conditions as printed** |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| Non-Warrantable Condo | 80% | 75% | 75% | “-5% CLTV for Florida properties, Min DSCR: 1.0” |
| Condotel / PUDtel | 75% | 70% | 65% | “-5% CLTV for Florida properties Min DSCR: 1.0” |
| 2-4 Unit | 80% | 80% | 80% | Printed as “Max CLTV: 80%” with no purpose split |
| Manufactured Home | 65% | 60% | 60% | — |

STD-8.2 Above 80.00% LTV only SFR, Warrantable Condos outside of Florida, Townhome and PUD are eligible (STD-3.16). \[S: Income Documentation\]

STD-8.3 Rural / unique property: maximum CLTV 80% (purchase), 75% (refinance — rate & term), 70% (refinance — cash-out); minimum FICO 700; minimum DSCR 1.00. “If marketing time is excessive or property exhibits unusual, inadequate or peculiar functionality, LTV may be further reduced.” \[S: Subject Property Location\]

STD-8.4 Declining market: “-5% CLTV property/borrower full profile” (STD-1.14). \[S: Subject Property Location\]

proposals.reasoning: Checks only that the property type is one of the listed eligible types and that the state is not SD. The other source-clause requirements are not encoded.

  - All entities holding direct ownership of the subject property and on title as a direct owner are borrowing entities.
  - All individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% provide a recourse guarantee, Acra approved or Exhibit 7.
  - At least one guarantor has prior homeownership experience.
  - At least one borrower / guarantor attests on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

STD-6.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-22. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

STD-6.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. See Q-09. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

proposals.reasoning: Encodes only the check that Borrower.entity_documents_complete is true. Missing or unrecognized values are undecided. Entity type, title ownership, guarantees, homeownership experience, and all other reviewer checks are not evaluated.

rule.description: Python formalization of acra-standard.loan_program_eligibility.first_time_homebuyer_eligibility

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Verify the stated first-time homebuyer eligibility conditions for a DSCR loan.
PURPOSE: Determine whether a first-time homebuyer loan meets every stated DSCR condition.
CHECKS TO ENCODE:

  - If Borrower.is_first_time_homebuyer is true, LoanCore.cltv_percent is no more than 70%.
  - If Borrower.is_first_time_homebuyer is true, LoanCore.total_loan_amount_usd is no more than $1,000,000.
  - If Borrower.is_first_time_homebuyer is true, the loan is fully amortizing and is not interest-only.
CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER:

SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-4.9 “Acra defines a First Time Home Buyers (‘FTHB’) as an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property).” \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.10 DSCR: Acra allows first-time homebuyers under all of the following: minimum 700 FICO score; maximum 70% CLTV; minimum DSCR of 1.150; maximum loan amount of \$1,000,000; full amortization required, no interest-only programs; impounds required; minimum six months reserves. STD-4.12 §3.12 separately requires at least one guarantor with prior homeownership experience where the borrower is an entity (STD-6.9). How that requirement and the first-time-homebuyer allowance interact: Acra confirmation requested → Q-09.

proposals.reasoning: Applies the stated minimum 700 score, maximum 70% CLTV, maximum $1,000,000 loan amount, and no-interest-only condition only when the borrower is a first-time homebuyer. rule.description: Python formalization of acra-standard.loan_program_eligibility.foreign_national_eligibility

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Verify the Foreign National residence, business-purpose, and investment-property requirements and apply the stated leverage limits.
PURPOSE: Determine whether a Foreign National borrower meets the requirements stated for Foreign National financing.
CHECKS TO ENCODE:
  - If Borrower.citizenship_status is Foreign National, the borrower resides outside of the U.S.
  - If Borrower.citizenship_status is Foreign National, the transaction is a business purpose transaction on investment property.
  - If Borrower.citizenship_status is Foreign National, LoanCore.cltv_percent is no more than 70% for purchase or 65% for rate & term or cash-out refinance.
CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER:
  - If Borrower.citizenship_status is Foreign National, the loan is priced at FICO equal to 700.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident, Non-Permanent Resident, Foreign National, ITIN. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.3 Non-Permanent Resident must have proof of legal residency, which may include an unexpired employment authorization document (EAD) or valid visa. Limit printed as “Max Loan Amount: \$1.5M: Max CLTV 80%” — whether this is two independent limits or one conditional limit: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.4 Foreign National: “Borrowers whose Primary Residence is not located in the United States of America.” Maximum CLTV 70% (purchase) and 65% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out); “Price loan at FICO equal to 700”. No maximum loan amount is stated for foreign nationals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. Program documentation is in section 5. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.5 ITIN: “ITIN is defined as any non-resident that is unable to provide any of the ‘Non-Permanent Resident Alien’ documents listed above.” Maximum loan amount \$1.0M; minimum FICO 640; maximum CLTV by FICO as printed below. §3.10 separately admits ITIN holders under the foreign-national program when they reside outside the US. Whether a US-resident ITIN holder is eligible, and whether the tier printed “FICO 700” means 700 and above: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[S: Borrower Citizenship; G §3.10, p. 6\]

| **ITIN tier as printed** | **Purchase** | **Refinance — R/T and cash-out** |
|--------------------------|--------------|----------------------------------|
| “FICO 700”               | 70%          | 65%                              |
| “FICO 660 to 699”        | 65%          | 60%                              |
| “FICO 640 to 659”        | 60%          | 60%                              |

STD-5.1 Foreign Nationals are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions only (i.e. investment properties). \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.2 Eligible under the Foreign National Program are Non-Resident Aliens who are not authorized to live or work in the U.S. “A true Foreign National may periodically visit the U.S. for various reasons including vacation and / or business, may purchase property for limited personal use or investment, or may own a U.S based business entity, but they must reside outside of the U.S.” \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.3 Borrowers who are holders of Individual Tax Identification Numbers (ITIN) are eligible for this program if they reside outside of the U.S. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.4 “Due to market exchange rates, applicants are to be reviewed with scrutiny toward a post-close financial position and their ability to mitigate exchange rate fluctuations.” \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.5 “See 3.10 for OFAC restrictions and state specific exclusions” — not reproduced (Appendix B). \[G §3.10, p. 7\]

proposals.reasoning: For Foreign Nationals, the source defines the category by a primary residence outside the U.S.; the allowed fields provide no separate residence field. The source permits Foreign National financing only for business-purpose transactions (i.e. investment properties), represented here by SubjectProperty.occupancy_subtype. The CLTV limits are 70 for purchase and 65 for rate-and-term or cash-out refinance. FICO pricing is left to the reviewer and is not checked.

rule.description: Python formalization of acra-standard.loan_program_eligibility.interest_only_eligibility

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Apply the stated interest-only loan amount, credit score, term-specific CLTV, and availability restrictions.
PURPOSE: Determine whether an interest-only loan meets its applicable product requirements and restrictions.
CHECKS TO ENCODE:
  - If MortgageLoanInformation.is_interest_only is true, LoanCore.total_loan_amount_usd is at least $250,000.
  - If MortgageLoanInformation.is_interest_only is true, CreditReport.representative_score is at least 640.
  - If MortgageLoanInformation.is_interest_only is true and LoanCore.is_interest_only_10_40 is true, LoanCore.cltv_percent is no more than 80%.
  - If Borrower.is_first_time_homebuyer is true, interest-only is not selected.
  - If SubjectProperty.is_vacant is true and LoanCore.loan_purpose is refinance, interest-only is not selected.
  - If SubjectProperty.listed_for_sale_last_6_months is true, interest-only is not selected.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-2.5 Loan amount \< \$200,000: maximum CLTV 80% (purchase) and 75% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out). \[S: Loan Amount\]

STD-2.6 Loan amount \> \$2,000,000: must have 1.0 or greater DSCR. \[S: Loan Amount\]

STD-2.7 Interest-only loans: minimum loan amount \$250,000; maximum loan amount \$3,000,000; minimum FICO 640. Product-level interest-only conditions are in section 10. \[S: Loan Amount\]

STD-4.9 “Acra defines a First Time Home Buyers (‘FTHB’) as an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property).” \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.10 DSCR: Acra allows first-time homebuyers under all of the following: minimum 700 FICO score; maximum 70% CLTV; minimum DSCR of 1.150; maximum loan amount of \$1,000,000; full amortization required, no interest-only programs; impounds required; minimum six months reserves. The Summary states the same conditions: “Minimum 700 FICO: Max 70% CLTV: DSCR ≥ 1.15: Loan amt ≤ \$1MM: NO I/O: Must Impound: Requires 6mos Reserves”. \[G §3.13, p. 10; S: Restrictions\]

STD-4.11 “Where a FTHB is purchasing an Investment property and the loan is qualifying via DTI program, the maximum DTI will be 43.0%.” Noted as a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.12 §3.12 separately requires at least one guarantor with prior homeownership experience where the borrower is an entity (STD-6.9). How that requirement and the first-time-homebuyer allowance interact: Acra confirmation requested → Q-09.

STD-8.5 A vacant property may be purchased; qualifying rents are taken from the 1007 or 1025 (STD-3.8). “Vacant investment properties are only eligible for a refinance transaction if consistent with §10.17.” \[G §5.32, p. 3; §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-8.6 Rate and term refinance of a vacant property (§10.17): minimum 700 FICO score; maximum \$1,000,000 to maximum 70% CLTV; maximum \$2,000,000 to maximum 65% CLTV; minimum 1.000 DSCR or maximum 40.0% DTI (Q-14); minimum two-year prepayment penalty (where allowable); full amortization required, no interest-only programs; impounds required; minimum six months reserves. The Summary states the same conditions with “Max CLTV 70% for loan amounts under \$1,000,000 and 65% for loan amounts under \$2,000,000”. Treatment at exactly \$1,000,000 and \$2,000,000: Acra confirmation requested → Q-10. \[G §10.17, p. 11; S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-8.7 Cash-out refinance of a vacant property: the “Cash-Out Refinances” heading in §10.17 is empty in the excerpt. The Summary states: minimum 700 FICO; DSCR ≥ 1.15; ≥ 3-year PPP (where allowable); no interest only; impounds required; 6 months reserves; “Max CLTV 60% for loan amounts under \$1,500,000”; “Requires ≥15 months ownership”. Loans of \$1,500,000 or more, and how the 15 months are measured: Acra confirmation requested → Q-10. \[S: Occupancy Type; G §10.17, p. 11\]

STD-8.8 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

STD-8.9 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI (Q-14); a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

STD-10.1 Eligible product types: 30 Yr Fixed; 5/1 ARM; 7/1 ARM; Interest Only (5 Yr / 30 year term, available on 5/1 or 7/1 ARM); Interest Only (5 Yr / 30 Year Fixed); Interest Only (10 Yr / 40 Year Term). \[S: Product Requirements\]

STD-10.2 ARM requirements: Index 1 Yr CMT; Caps 2/2/6; Margin 3.00 (FICO 760+), 3.25 (FICO 720-759), 3.50 (FICO 700-719), 3.75 (FICO 680-699), 4.00 (FICO 660-679), 4.25 (FICO 640-659), 5.00 (FICO 600-639). \[S: Product Requirements\]

STD-10.3 Interest Only, 5 Yr / 30 Year Fixed or 5/1 and 7/1 ARM: minimum loan ≥ \$250K; minimum 640 credit score. \[S: Product Requirements\]

STD-10.4 Interest Only, 10 Yr / 40 Year Term: minimum loan ≥ \$250K; minimum 640 credit score; maximum 80% LTV / CLTV; maximum \$3M loan amount. \[S: Product Requirements\]

STD-10.5 Interest-only is not available to first-time homebuyers (STD-4.10), on vacant-property refinances (STD-8.6 and 8.7) or on properties listed for sale (STD-8.9). \[G §3.13, §10.17, §11.5\]

STD-10.6 Interest Only payments are calculated as the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest on the mortgage monthly at the time of origination, usually for a set term at the beginning of the repayment term; after that term the payments are recast to a fully amortized payment for the balance of the term ending at maturity. Acra calculates the DSCR using the first payment due under the Note (STD-3.2; which payment enters the denominator on an interest-only loan is Q-26). The excerpt's DTI calculation for interest-only loans (first fully amortized payment on the original balance; for an ARM, the highest achievable rate at that payment's due date) is a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §7.5, p. 13\]

proposals.reasoning: Encodes only the listed interest-only checks: minimum $250,000 loan amount, minimum 640 representative score, maximum 80% CLTV for the 10-year/40-year option, and the stated first-time-homebuyer, vacant-property refinance, and recent-listing restrictions. The conditional fields are read only when needed; an unstated relevant value yields rules_lib.unknown rather than a failure. Other source-clause requirements, including the $3,000,000 maximum, are not added because they are not among the checks requested.

rule.description: Python formalization of acra-standard.loan_program_eligibility.investment_occupancy

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Determine whether the subject property meets the program's investment-property occupancy requirement.
PURPOSE: Establish that the property is investment property and is not owner occupied.

  - SubjectProperty.occupancy_subtype is investment / non-owner occupied.
CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER:
  - The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence by individuals other than the owner.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
The Standard DSCR program finances loans on investment property, qualified on the subject property's rent rather than the borrower's income; whether every loan is a business-purpose transaction is Q-27. This section collects the program-level requirements that apply before any matrix or overlay is consulted.

STD-1.1 Occupancy is investment property (non-owner occupied) only. \[S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (STD-9.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

STD-1.4 The matrix columns are Purchase, Rate & Term and Cash-Out. Delayed financing is addressed only by the matrix footnote “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”. Which column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-06. \[S: matrix and footnote\]

STD-1.5 A loan qualifies either by a calculated DSCR (§5.32) or as No Ratio DSCR, where no ratio is calculated (§5.33). Both are set out in section 3. \[G §5.32–5.33, p. 3\]

STD-1.6 “Borrowing entity income documentation not required.” Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. \[S: Income Documentation; G §7.3, p. 5\]

proposals.reasoning: Encodes only the stated investment (non-owner occupied) subtype requirement. Whether the dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence is left to a reviewer.

condition.source:
import rules_lib


def check(ctx):
    loan_amount = ctx['LoanCore.total_loan_amount_usd']
    property_type = ctx['SubjectProperty.property_type']
    number_of_units = ctx['SubjectProperty.number_of_units']
    cltv = ctx['LoanCore.cltv_percent']

    missing = rules_lib.gaps(
        loan_amount=loan_amount,
        property_type=property_type,
        number_of_units=number_of_units,
        cltv=cltv,
    )
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    cap_applies = (
        loan_amount < 350000
        or loan_amount > 1500000
        or rules_lib.same(property_type, 'Warrantable Condo', 'Two-Units')
        or number_of_units == 2
        or rules_lib.same(number_of_units, '2')
    )
    return not cap_applies or cltv <= 75.00

  - Where an account serving as the source of funds must be verified, its source is verified by the stated bank statement(s) or VOD.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
PLAT-8.1 Gift funds, investment property: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price (PLAT-1.15). \[G §8.7, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction is Q-22. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing”. Foreign nationals are not eligible for this program, but an eligible US citizen or permanent resident may hold funds abroad; the same sentence's 60-day seasoning requirement is stated for Foreign Nationals only and is not restated. Whether the repatriation requirement applies to eligible borrowers holding funds abroad, and what evidence and timing convention apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.6 “See guidelines for unacceptable source of funds” — the Seller's Guide provision is not reproduced (Appendix B). \[P: Reserve Requirements\]

proposals.reasoning: The clause triggers only above 70% CLTV. At or below 70%, neither listed condition applies. Above 70%, the permitted fields provide neither funds-to-close amount (needed to apply the business-purpose $50,000 threshold) nor evidence that seasoning verification was provided. The permitted fields also do not reliably identify consumer-transaction status; the code therefore returns cannot-tell rather than treating missing information as a failure. In the cases above 70%, `satisfied: false` means the requirement cannot be affirmed from the permitted inputs, not that the case is known to fail. The $50,000 threshold cannot be tested with the allowed fields.

SOURCE CLAUSE: One matrix covers all loan amounts to \$2,000,000. It is reproduced below exactly as printed, followed by its footnotes in Acra's words. The printed FICO thresholds are 730, 721 and 700, which leaves a score of exactly 720 to be read literally; the reading and its consequences are set out for Acra to confirm rather than adopted. PLAT-2.1 The rows below are Acra's. Each row is a minimum-FICO threshold: a score at or above the threshold and below the next higher threshold takes that row. No row is printed below 700. \[P: Loan Amount, FICO, CLTV Requirements\] | **Min FICO** | **Purchase** | **Rate & Term** | **Cash-Out** | |--------------|--------------|-----------------|--------------| | 730 | 80% | 80% | 75% | | 721 | 80% | 80% | 65% | | 700 | 80% | 80% | 55% |

THE PRINTED 721 THRESHOLD AND A SCORE OF 720

Read literally, a decisioning score of 720 falls in the 700 row (cash-out maximum 55%), sits outside the Correspondent restriction printed for “700-719 FICO” (footnote 3), and takes the 3.25 ARM margin printed for “720-759”. This document does not normalize 721 to 720. Whether the 721 threshold is intended, and how 720 is treated on each of the three points: Acra confirmation requested → Q-01.

A score of exactly 720 is returned for Acra confirmation rather than decided, and scores below 700 have no printed row and are left undecided. rule.description: Python formalization of acra-platinum.identification_requirements.entity_documentation_package

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Verify the required entity documentation, including applicable entity-specific documents, name matching, authorizations, and any required qualifications.
PURPOSE: Verify the entity documents required by PLAT-5.10 and the related requirements in the Seller’s Guide excerpt.
CHECKS (encode those the case fields settle; leave the rest to a reviewer):
  - A complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation or Articles of Organization and all amendments is present.
  - For an LLC or Partnership, a complete, legible Operating Agreement with all referenced exhibits and amendments is present; for a corporation, a complete, legible set of Bylaws with all referenced exhibits and amendments is present; the applicable document states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers.
  - Documentation evidencing all ownership interests is present: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement identifies or attaches all persons by name with their ownership interest, or membership interest certificates or units are provided in compliance with the Operating Agreement.
  - For an S or C Corporation, shareholder or stockholder certificates complying with the Bylaws, if any, or the corporation’s stock ledger when certificates are lost or unavailable, accounts for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation or Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation; an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is present when stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable.
  - For an S-corporation or Partnership where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, the most recent preceding tax year’s K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest and a CPA or Tax Preparer letter affirming current ownership interest are present; if the preceding year’s taxes have not been filed, the letter includes a statement to that effect.
  - Names on the entity documents match the identification, or a letter of explanation addresses any discrepancy where the names do not match exactly.
  - A Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date is present.
  - If the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located, a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted is present.
  - An IRS Form SS4, Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity is present; if an EIN exception request is submitted, it includes a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds for review by Acra’s Legal Department.
  - A Unanimous Written Consent or Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest authorizes the transaction with Acra Lending and identifies who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity.
  - If a principal designates an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee, a Power of Attorney is utilized by the principal.
  - A borrower letter stating that a required document is not required, available, or excused from providing is not used as a substitute for that required document.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
PLAT-5.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

proposals.reasoning: The case fields provide a single entity-document completeness indicator. Use it to decide the check; the available fields do not separately establish document types, contents, name matching, authorizations, qualifications, or other individual requirements, so those remain for reviewer verification. No thresholds apply.

PLAT-7.8 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI — on this program the channel minimum DSCR applies, Wholesale 1.0 and Correspondent 1.2 (PLAT-3.8), and the DTI alternative is Q-14; a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

proposals.reasoning: The supplied field already states whether the property was listed within the six-month window, so there is no separate date threshold to calculate. If it was not listed, this prohibition is not triggered. If it was listed, the allowed fields do not state whether subordinate financing is present; the result is therefore unknown for reviewer assessment, not a failure. The second case is not established as satisfied (the function returns unknown), rather than being treated as a confirmed violation.
