rule.description: Python formalization of acra-platinum.loan_program_eligibility.entity_borrower_eligibility

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Verify that an entity borrower and its ownership structure meet the stated entity requirements.
PURPOSE: Determine whether an entity borrower meets the published entity eligibility requirements.
CHECKS (encode those the case fields settle; leave the rest to a reviewer):
  - The entity type and ownership structure are allowed by the program.
  - The entity is US formed and based, and an entity borrower meets the stated SPE requirements.
  - Every entity holding direct ownership of the subject property is a borrowing entity.
  - Each individual with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% provides a recourse guarantee.
  - No ownership change made to circumvent required personal guarantors is relied on if it occurred within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-18. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

proposals.reasoning: The available entity_type field can be used to check whether the stated type is among the types listed as allowed. A bare LLC type passes this type check only; whether it is single-purpose and non-series, US formed and based, and whether ownership, guarantees, and timing requirements are met cannot be established from the permitted fields and is left to a reviewer. The 20% ownership threshold and 30-day lookback are therefore not encoded; no thresholds are tested.

rule.description: Python formalization of acra-platinum.loan_program_eligibility.fico_and_matrix_cltv
citations: Acra_DSCR_Platinum_Select_Consolidated_Guidelines_v1_0 1.docx#2. Loan amount, FICO and maximum CLTV
Acra_DSCR_Platinum_Select_Consolidated_Guidelines_v1_0 1.docx#2.1 Matrix as printed — Loan Amount, FICO, CLTV Requirements

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Apply the printed FICO and purpose-specific CLTV matrix to the loan. PURPOSE: Determine whether the representative credit score and CLTV meet the published matrix requirements. CHECKS TO ENCODE: - The representative score is at least 700. CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER: - The CLTV does not exceed the matrix maximum for the loan purpose and representative-score row. - For a Correspondent loan with a score of 700-719, the CLTV does not exceed 60%. SOURCE CLAUSE: One matrix covers all loan amounts to \$2,000,000. It is reproduced below exactly as printed, followed by its footnotes in Acra's words. The printed FICO thresholds are 730, 721 and 700, which leaves a score of exactly 720 to be read literally; the reading and its consequences are set out for Acra to confirm rather than adopted. PLAT-2.1 The rows below are Acra's. Each row is a minimum-FICO threshold: a score at or above the threshold and below the next higher threshold takes that row. No row is printed below 700. \[P: Loan Amount, FICO, CLTV Requirements\] | **Min FICO** | **Purchase** | **Rate & Term** | **Cash-Out** | |--------------|--------------|-----------------|--------------| | 730 | 80% | 80% | 75% | | 721 | 80% | 80% | 65% | | 700 | 80% | 80% | 55% |

THE PRINTED 721 THRESHOLD AND A SCORE OF 720

Read literally, a decisioning score of 720 falls in the 700 row (cash-out maximum 55%), sits outside the Correspondent restriction printed for “700-719 FICO” (footnote 3), and takes the 3.25 ARM margin printed for “720-759”. This document does not normalize 721 to 720. Whether the 721 threshold is intended, and how 720 is treated on each of the three points: Acra confirmation requested → Q-01.
PLAT-2.2 Footnote 1, whose marker is printed on the Cash-Out column heading: “When LTV \> 65% Max Cash-in-Hand: \$1,000,000 for loans ≥ \$1,500,000, \$500,000 for loans \< \$1,500,000.” Footnote 2, whose marker appears nowhere in the matrix: “When LTV ≤ 65%, unlimited cash-in-hand allowed.” The footnotes are stated in LTV while the matrix is labelled CLTV: Acra confirmation requested → Q-16. \[P: matrix footnotes 1–2\] PLAT-2.3 Footnote 3, whose marker also appears nowhere in the matrix: “Correspondent Pricing limited to 60% CLTV for 700-719 FICO”. For a Correspondent cash-out at 700-719 the matrix already prints 55%; the 60% footnote does not raise that figure. How the two limits apply together by purpose: Acra confirmation requested → Q-01. \[P: matrix footnote 3\] PLAT-2.4 Footnote \*: “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM” (PLAT-1.4, Q-02). \[P: matrix footnote\]

proposals.reasoning: Encodes only the requirement that the representative score is at least 700. CLTV matrix limits and the Correspondent-specific limit are left to the reviewer, so no purpose or CLTV fields are read.

  - If the property was listed for sale within the last six months, it is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s).

  - If the property was listed for sale within the last six months, the prepayment penalty is at least three (3) years unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties.
  - If the property was listed for sale within the last six months, LTV / CLTV is no more than 65% based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price.
  - If the property was listed for sale within the last six months, impounds are in place.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
PLAT-7.6 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

PLAT-7.7 Whether §11.5 applies to Platinum Select unchanged is part of Q-13; it is restated here because the Platinum Summary does not exclude it. \[G §11.5\]

PLAT-7.8 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI — on this program the channel minimum DSCR applies, Wholesale 1.0 and Correspondent 1.2 (PLAT-3.8), and the DTI alternative is Q-14; a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

proposals.reasoning: For listed properties, the encoded checks require at least 24 months of reserves, a non-interest-only loan, and—when the occupancy subtype identifies an investment property—a current tenant lease and non-vacant status. The clause does not provide a permitted case field for subordinate financing, so a listed case that passes the available checks is returned as cannot tell rather than being treated as satisfied. The listed cases at 24 and 25 months therefore are not established as satisfied. Reviewer-only checks are not evaluated.

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Determine whether the subject property satisfies Platinum Select's non-owner-occupied investment-property requirements.
PURPOSE: Determine whether the subject property meets the program's occupancy and vacancy requirements.
CHECKS TO ENCODE:
  - The subject property is not vacant.
CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER:
  - The subject property is non-owner occupied.
  - The subject property is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence by individuals other than the owner.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
Platinum Select finances loans on non-owner occupied property, qualified on the subject property's rent, within a narrower box than the Standard program; whether every loan is a business-purpose transaction is Q-22. This section collects the program-level requirements that apply before the matrix or any condition is consulted.

PLAT-1.1 Occupancy: Non-Owner Occupied. \[P: Occupancy Requirements\]

PLAT-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” The property types the Platinum Summary lists as eligible are at PLAT-7.1; types it does not list are set out in the table at 7.1 and asked in Q-07. \[G §3.41, p. 11; P: Subject Property Requirements\]

PLAT-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR Platinum” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (PLAT-8.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-22. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

PLAT-1.4 Eligible loan purpose types: Purchase, Rate & Term Refinance, Cash-Out Refinance, Delayed Financing. The matrix footnote states “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”; which matrix column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02. \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements; matrix footnote\]

PLAT-1.5 “Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) Cash-Out Refinance Transactions requires current lease agreement”. \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements\]

PLAT-1.6 “Vacant properties ineligible”. The Seller's Guide provisions on vacant purchases and §10.17 vacant refinances therefore do not apply (Appendix B). \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements\]

PLAT-7.5 Vacant properties are ineligible (PLAT-1.6). The §10.17 vacant-refinance provisions and the §5.32 rule for qualifying rent on a vacant purchase are not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements\]

proposals.reasoning: The only check to encode is that the subject property is not vacant. A missing or uninterpretable vacancy value is undecided. Non-owner occupancy and the lease-and-principal-residence requirements are left to a reviewer and do not affect this function.

condition.source:
import rules_lib


def check(ctx):
    entity_type = ctx['Borrower.entity_type']
    missing = rules_lib.gaps(entity_type=entity_type)
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    excluded = rules_lib.same(
        entity_type,
        'Series LLC',
        'Cooperative',
        'Irrevocable Trust',
        'Land Trust',
        'IRA',
        'Non-Profit',
        'Joint Venture',
    )
    allowed = rules_lib.same(
        entity_type,
        'Domestic Corporation',
        'C Corp',
        'S Corp',
        'Single Purpose Limited Liability Company',
        'LLC',
        'Limited Liability Company',
        'LLP',
        'Limited Liability Partnership',
        'LLLP',
        'Limited Liability Limited Partnership',
        'GP',
        'General Partnership',
        'LP',
        'Limited Partnership',
        'Sole Proprietorship',
    )
    return bool(allowed and not excluded)

rule.description: Python formalization of acra-platinum.title_review.entity_borrower_eligibility

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Verify that an entity borrower and its entity structure meet the stated entity eligibility requirements.
PURPOSE: Determine whether the entity borrower, its entity type, formation, structure, and use of the property meet the stated eligibility rules.
CHECKS TO ENCODE:
  - The entity type is allowed and is not a series LLC, Cooperative, Irrevocable Trust, Land Trust, IRA, Non-Profit, or Joint Venture.
CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER:
  - For an entity borrower, the transaction is a business purpose transaction and the property is an investment property.
  - The entity borrower is a single purpose entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties and is engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.
  - The entity is a US formed and based Entity and is not a foreign entity or foreign owned entity.
  - Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn is owned by individual(s), with no multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera.
  - Title to the collateral is held directly by individual person(s) or by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-18. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

proposals.reasoning: Checks only whether the stated entity type is among the types allowed by PLAT-5.7 and is not one of the expressly excluded types in PLAT-5.8. Missing entity type information returns an unknown verdict. No numerical thresholds apply. SPE status, transaction purpose, property use, formation, ownership structure, and title acceptability are left to a reviewer as directed.
